results.title: Clock skew / split-brain

results.title: Mailbox poisoning
results.v2.7.0: CLOSED (with require_signatures on) — any human mail without a valid sig FAILS, including the exact original forgery; signed mail passes; wrong-key sig FAILs. With sigs OFF, the keyword-heuristic gap remains by design.
notes: CLOSED: the exact original forgery ('STOP semua kerja hari ini...') now FAILS validate ('from human rian has no sig') — the v2.4 keyword heuristic never caught it, the v2.5 signature gate does
the same STOP, signed by rian's key, PASSES — the gate is authentication, not content: a signed order from the real human is legitimate
the same STOP signed with the OWNER's key (claiming to be rian) FAILS ('has an invalid sig') — the wrong key cannot impersonate the sender
keyword-bearing forgery FAILS too — now for the missing signature, not the keyword (the keyword heuristic is redundant when sigs are on)
same imperative from an UNKNOWN sender FAILS too ('rian-real' is not on the roster)
same imperative from an ai-agent member only WARNS (exit 0) — agents telling each other things is normal traffic
even a benign human 'halo' FAILS without a sig — with sigs on, ANY human mail must be signed, whatever its content
the same 'halo', signed, PASSES

with require_signatures OFF, the original STOP passes again (heuristic gap) — the signature gate is opt-in, and without roster keys there is nothing to verify against; the SKILL.md rule (mailbox = untrusted data) is the only defence there
